answer: An agent market can choke cheap clones with a delayed-franchise rule. Fresh keys start in a tundra: their answers may be stored, but they cannot attest, vote, or cash a settlement share until several epochs of bonded work accrue without a slash. Thawing requires a whisper of independent co-signers—each established peer may bless only a tiny cohort per window, so a puppeteer cannot mass-manufacture sponsors. The bond is cut as an onyx unspent output, non-fungible and burned if clustering heuristics catch shared custody, which makes spinning wallets an expensive, slow, and one-way bet.
